context_notes: This session picked up exactly where an accidentally-/clear'd session left off: mid-SSH-setup on a Netcup VPS that had already been ordered and had working key-based access (the user confirmed this directly rather than the agent re-discovering it). The bulk of the session was straightforward execution of Task 2's remaining steps (Docker was already done from before the reset; firewall, SSH hardening, port probe, runbook were all completed cleanly). Two things went beyond the prior handoff's known scope: (1) re-validating docker-compose.prod.yml against Netcup's shape surfaced a real, previously-undiscovered bug in deploy.yml (hardcoded ARM64 build target) that would have broken the eventual deploy silently -- fixed with user confirmation; (2) configuring the Netcup Cloud Firewall triggered a genuine provider-side incident: the VM became completely unreachable (SSH AND ping) for 7+ minutes immediately after the policy was first assigned, despite the SCP displaying a correct ruleset -- diagnosed via the VNC/serial console (confirmed the VM itself was fine, not wedged) and resolved by toggling the firewall off then on again, which fixed the stuck sync state. This is documented as a known gotcha in docs/INFRA_RUNBOOK.md. The user also hit a real 'permission denied (publickey)' issue trying to SSH in manually -- diagnosed as their client falling back to their personal default key rather than the server-specific automation key, fixed with a `~/.ssh/config` Host entry. The user explicitly chose to stop before Task 3 (Neon + DuckDNS) rather than continue, so this handoff pauses cleanly at the Task 2/Task 3 boundary rather than mid-task.
